text:
sarah_cs: Hey team, customer on account redwood-enterprise reported streaming responses getting cut mid-output. They reconnect and sometimes see the model re-generate the tail, resulting in duplicated phrases and extra tokens charged. Repro steps attached.

raj_support: thx Sarah — do we have a sample request id / session id? which SDK?

sarah_cs: They used our vanilla JS SDK, v1.4.1. Session id in logs: sess_7G2m. Root request ts: 1799854321. Repro steps: 1) start streaming request for ~800-token completion 2) kill client network after 3s 3) reconnect with client resume logic sending last_event_id they got 4) server streams remainder but sometimes replays ~50 tokens from the end, or sends both remainder and a full re-generation.

mike_backend: looking through runtime logs for sess_7G2m. I see two distinct generation traces: gen_id g_9fa and g_9fb within 200ms of reconnect. Both consumed tokens. From the runtime perspective we received two create requests that look almost identical.

raj_support: so client sent two requests? Did it retry without idempotency token?

mike_backend: client did not provide an idempotency token header. Their reconnect path is "resume by Last-Event-ID" then if resume fails they retry a fresh request. But because resume sometimes succeeds partially, the client code falls into a race and issues a redundant create. We're treating Last-Event-ID as advisory and also re-issuing a new generation.

alex_infra: quick note: our SSE resume semantics currently accept Last-Event-ID and will attempt to seek KV-cache cursor by that event id. But if the event id points to a partial chunk not yet checkpointed server-side, we trigger a fallback new generation. That fallback path currently does not check for idempotency-token -> new generation created.

raj_support: customer upset about unexpected billing for duplicate tokens. Any quick mitigation?

mike_backend: couple options:
- short term: add a duplicate-detection window in the top layer keyed by (customer_id, prompt_hash, approx_start_seq) for 2 minutes, drop/mark second generation as dedup and refund billing by flagging the record. quick patch.
- preferred: require or strongly encourage idempotency-token on client retries and honor duplicate suppression if same token seen within TTL. Also make resume logic return explicit resume_token that is authoritative and tied to a generation id.

alex_infra: I'll sketch a server change: on create we return a streaming session object with fields: resume_token, generation_id. Reconnects must send resume_token in Last-Event-ID or Resume header. If server sees a resume_token for an existing active generation it attaches to that generation; if client retries without resume_token but with idempotency-token we map to existing generation. If neither present, create new generation. Also we should add per-event seq numbers to SSE so clients can detect overlap.

raj_support: can you paste the logs where we saw both gens?

mike_backend: pasted below (redacted):

```
[1799854321.112] sess=sess_7G2m create gen=g_9fa prompt_hash=0x7b2 start_seq=0
[1799854324.520] sess=sess_7G2m disconnect client=203.0.113.12
[1799854324.700] sess=sess_7G2m reconnect attempt by client without resume_token
[1799854324.702] sess=sess_7G2m create gen=g_9fb prompt_hash=0x7b2 start_seq=0
[1799854330.010] gen=g_9fa sent event seq=0..220
[1799854330.011] gen=g_9fb sent event seq=0..230
```

raj_support: that matches. So server accepted a second create at reconnect because no resume_token/idempotency.

sarah_cs: customer code path: when network blip happens they call sdk.streamResume(lastEventId) which does this client-side pseudo:

```
if (!lastEventId) {
  api.createStream(payload)
} else {
  api.resumeStream({ lastEventId }).catch(_ => api.createStream(payload))
}
```

No idempotency token anywhere.

mike_backend: client pattern is racy: if resume succeeds and also the SDK falls into catch path due to websocket timeout, it may create. We need SDK changes too: when calling createStream as fallback, include idempotency token equal to lastEventId or a stable request UUID so server can dedup.

alex_infra: infra tasks:
- enforce resume_token generation on create (small runtime change)
- add server-side dedupe TTL keyed by (customer, idempotency_token) and by (resume_token->generation_id) for 5m
- extend billing export so duplicates with dedupe flag don't escalate billing

raj_support: for the customer immediate workaround, can we ask them to pin SDK to next patch or apply a client-side guard: only one outstanding create/resume per session, and generate an idempotency token for fallback using lastEventId or GUID?

sarah_cs: yes, already suggested that to them. They asked about partial outputs where resume reproduces overlapping tokens e.g., last 20 tokens repeated — will sequence numbers help?

mike_backend: yes. If each SSE event includes monotonic seq number offset (token_index) relative to generation start, client can drop any event with seq <= last_seq it has. Example SSE payload header: "event: chunk\n id: <resume_token>\n seq: 123\n data: ...". We'll add header field `X-Redwood-Event-Seq` for HTTP-based resumes too.

alex_infra: I'll open infra ticket and patch. Quick patch planned: return resume_token on create, enforce resume_token in resume path, and add dedupe TTL. I'll also coordinate billing team for credits.

billing-bot: noted refund request queued: ticket REF-8321 created, flagged urgent.

deploy-bot: canary rollout for resume_token change scheduled to eng-runtime channel at 1799860000, will be gradual.

raj_support: action items for support: 1) tell customer to upgrade SDK patch (we'll give a hand-patched bundle) 2) confirm we will audit billing for duplicates and proactively credit obvious dup gens 3) include sample client guard snippet.

sarah_cs: I've communicated workaround and told them we'll follow up after infra patch. I'll attach their repro script. Will escalate if they don't see credits. Thanks all. :pray:

mike_backend: follow-up: I'll add explicit example headers for SDK:
```
Resume-Token: rt_abc123  # authoritative
Idempotency-Key: id_...   # stable per logical request
X-Last-Seq: 220          # optional client hint
```
Server logic pseudocode:
```
if resume_token present:
  attach to generation if generation.active
elif idempotency_key seen within TTL:
  return existing generation
else:
  create new generation
```

alex_infra: ticket created INFRA-2045 with detailed plan. leaving thread open for notes.

sarah_cs: closing loop with customer today, will post outcome here.
